# mtncloud_mos_bucket (Resource)

A bucket in MTN Object Storage (MOS), registered in the console under Infrastructure > Storage > Buckets so it can be used there too. The provider uses the tenant's MOS keys from Cypher: order "MTN Object Storage (MOS)" from the catalog once before using it. Destroy deletes the bucket in MOS and its console record. It refuses while an archive uses the bucket (deleting the record would delete the archive), and while the bucket holds objects unless `force_destroy` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A bucket, listed in the console under Infrastructure > Storage > Buckets.
resource "mtncloud_mos_bucket" "backups" {
  name          = "acme-backups"
  console_name  = "Acme backups"
  force_destroy = false # destroy fails while it holds objects
}

# A bucket whose objects can be kept from deletion (it can't be turned off later).
resource "mtncloud_mos_bucket" "records" {
  name                = "acme-records"
  object_lock_enabled = true
}

output "endpoint" {
  value = mtncloud_mos_bucket.backups.endpoint_url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The bucket's name in MOS: 3 to 63 lower-case letters, digits, dots and hyphens. Names are shared by every tenant on MOS. Changing it replaces the bucket, and its objects are lost.

### Optional

- `console_name` (String) The bucket's name in the console. Defaults to `name` when the bucket is created; removing it later keeps the current console name. Changing it renames the record in place.
- `endpoint` (String) Which MOS endpoint the console record uses: `public` (the default, reachable from anywhere) or `private` (from inside MTN Cloud only). Changing it updates the record in place.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, delete every object in the bucket first. Without it, destroying a bucket that holds objects fails. Objects under retention can't be deleted until it ends.
- `object_lock_enabled` (Boolean) Create the bucket with object lock, so objects can be kept from deletion for a retention period (`mtncloud_mos_bucket_object_lock`, `mtncloud_mos_object`). It can only be set when the bucket is created, and never turned off: changing it replaces the bucket. Needs object lock to be enabled on MTN Object Storage; the create fails with a clear message when it isn't.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `endpoint_url` (String) The endpoint's URL, for S3-compatible tools (path-style addressing).
- `id` (String) The console bucket record's ID.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the console record's ID
terraform import mtncloud_mos_bucket.backups 712
# or by the bucket's name
terraform import mtncloud_mos_bucket.backups acme-backups
```
